output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs comes mainly from inside Brackenford, not from Haverlow. Haverlow's trailer data shows loads arriving at 2–3.5°C with no trend. Trailers were empty about 23:00, but receipt was confirmed 02:30–03:00. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (week 31), median night dock-to-chamber time rose from 44 minutes to nearly 4 hours. Pallets sit on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Night write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9% across all suppliers, while day-shift rates stayed flat. The chambers held temperature. The "warm arrival" probe readings are taken after the dock wait, so they don't show the condition of the product on the trailer. Don't raise the chargeback or shift volume to Pellridge. Dropping the night probe would hide the problem. Restore night staffing, or otherwise fix the dock-to-chamber time, and set a maximum time monitored weekly from scan data. The rise in Corriebank credits (self-certification from 3 Aug) is a separate, smaller matter. Its cause is unproven, so pull a sample of claims and reconcile them before changing credit terms. Confidence is fairly high on the main finding, moderate on the credits.
output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check (GM's probe data is keyed after dock wait; vendor and GM both interested), then Kepner-Tregoe IS/IS NOT (night vs day, Haverlow vs other suppliers), then ACH across H1–H5.
